authoring.basis: Source-informed acceptance, frozen before candidate descriptions, graph results or implementation outcomes are acquired.
sourcesRead: Actual source and compiled-workflow addition metadata
authoring.limitations: The original source and both compiled workflow blobs are not in the read-only cache. They must be acquired and verified before assessing source-era applicability. Any outcome-informed revision must preserve this predecessor.

goal: For workflows declaring cache-memory, independently demonstrate useful corrections to avoidable cache misses or misconfigured cache restoration over time.

partialAcceptance.meaning: An independently verified compiled cache-memory restoration gains a fallback that no longer depends on the current run ID. This establishes a source-defined structural configuration repair, not an observed cache hit, work avoided, or time or credit saving.
before: An immutable source declares cache-memory and its immutable compiled workflow contains an unambiguously identified cache restore action over the cache-memory directory.
The primary key contains one direct github.run_id expression and a nonempty stable prefix.
The restoration has no restore-keys fallback.
after: The actual first parent is the before endpoint, and the independently dated delivered commit is the after endpoint.
The same source still declares cache-memory and the same compiled job, restore step identity, paths, primary key and execution constraints survive.
The restore-keys field gains the literal symbolic prefix preceding github.run_id in the unchanged primary key; that prefix has no run ID, run number, timestamp or mutable step-output dependency.
The frozen action implementation independently supports this fallback operation. Unsupported action versions, ambiguous syntax or missing source are unavailable, not accepted.
partialAcceptance.deduplication: Count a distinct repository, delivered commit, workflow path, job and restore-step repair once in its half-open delivery period. Multiple issue references or report snapshots do not multiply the repair.
partialAcceptance.scope: This narrow facet does not assess stable-key replacements, stale-data correctness, cache writes, hit-rate trends, all caching modes or full analyzer acceptance.

fullAcceptance.status: separate and unmeasured until independent evidence exists
requirements: Original cache read/write and restoration observations
Correct independent eligible-run population and cache-hit/miss interpretation
Useful repeated-work reduction without stale-data or correctness regressions

contribution: A current editable marker and dated downstream graph can corroborate shared contribution, not original issue publication or exclusive causation. Stronger numeric attribution requires original run/source/application receipts.
unknown: Missing originals, unsupported scope and incomplete empty populations remain null. A checked facet with no accepted repair is not zero whole-workflow value.

acquisition.roots: All surviving pre-cutoff issue/PR identities marked daily-cache-strategy-analyzer in the shared frozen history; freeze their ordered identity digest before reading descriptions.
acquisition.relationships: Bounded original same-repository connected/cross-referenced PR events, retaining pagination completeness and event times. Incomplete graph traversal must remain explicit.
acquisition.authority: Verify repository ID and public visibility before source or outcome reads. Read-only GitHub acquisition only; no dispatch, target execution, shared-cache writes, policy changes or publication.
acquisition.persistence: Retain digest-checked original response bytes and independently verified Git source bytes. Reuse completed exact-scope requests on resume.

decision: Not rated; no approved native keep bar.
